_comment: Which shipped config keys decide whether a plugin can do any work in a given repo.
ecosystem-449.28. Wave readiness asks 'has this plugin produced write-path events
in the target repo?', and a plugin sitting at zero reads as a stalled wave. But some
plugins cannot produce events in some repos at all: cartographer's undocumented_entity
check needs entity directories to walk, and a repo with none would leave it enabled,
green, and measuring nothing -- the exact Wave 0 failure where inspector shipped
checks:{}. Readiness needs to tell 'not yet' from 'not hostable here' before it can
mean anything.
The original motivating case was echo.watch_paths (ecosystem-449.15), which matched
agent and skill files the soak target did not have. Echo's stop gate was retired in
ONL-103 and its watch_paths went with it, so the entry is gone -- but the mechanism
it motivated is unchanged.
Inclusion globs answer that question: if none of them match a file in the target repo,
the plugin has no inputs there. Exclusion globs do not -- a skip list matching nothing
means nothing is skipped, which is a perfectly working plugin. That difference is
semantic, so it cannot be inferred from the config and has to be declared.
Every glob-bearing config key must appear in one of the two lists below.
test/node/check-repo-shaped-coverage.test.mjs fails on any that appears in neither,
so a new plugin cannot quietly skip the question. Same contract as
test/bus-coverage.json, for the same reason.

cartographer.why: The undocumented_entity check needs entity directories to walk. Its CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md audit still has targets anywhere, so cartographer is only partially inapplicable -- see the note in ecosystem-449.28.

excluded.compass.skip_globs: Exclusion list. Matching nothing means nothing is skipped, not that compass is inapplicable.
